how: The surviving flag proposal calls for joint work, while a later neighbouring-heart attempt explicitly invites help.

A participant asks for confirmation of the pan colours and receives the requested explanation.
The accommodating overlap exchange establishes neither shared room membership nor withdrawal under strain.

Participants propose a pan flag and fill a rainbow heart.
Members report starting and adding to the work, and the opener praises progress.

The final celebration also recounts covering, feared loss, and survival.

Organising messages do not establish the proposed flood and containment mechanism.

Reported cooperation by other groups does not establish a pan upkeep-to-coalition transition.
Admitted overlapping conversion does not preserve a call to turn the room's hands against a known rival.

The announced deal is not explicitly linked to a preserved call by this room to attack.
A recollection of covering does not establish a chain from this room's attack to continued rivalry talk.
Avoiding a fight motivates a fresh attempt without a stated judgment that too few hands forced the move.
Completion and pride share an edited passage, so they establish an association without a separately timed causal transition.
Celebration and reporting the work's fate share one turn, leaving a causal sequence from celebration to preservation unestablished.
The final account offers no observed decision to carry the effort forward after recounting survival.
The agreement preserves neither a post-agreement refusal nor a disclaimer made while accepting terms, leaving the bounded arrow untestable.
Confirming the other participant's colour question and praising their work repairs relations after the objection about wiping an overlooked community out.
Overlapping conversion establishes deliberate attack on a known rival only when recognition of the prior maker and hostile intention are supported.
A stated wish to avoid fighting can motivate another location without a claim of insufficient manpower.
A new attempt and an announced relocation deal establish a completed move only when completion is separately supported.
A temporary substitute on a neighbour's mark bridges a territorial dispute and promised later relocation.
